An oak tree grows slowly over many years. First, a squirrel buries an acorn and forgets it. Then, with rain and sun, the acorn sprouts into a tiny seedling. Over many years the seedling grows into a towering oak. Finally, that oak drops its own acorns, and the cycle begins again.

Describe the sequence, and explain how the ending connects back to the beginning.
items.answer: First a squirrel buries an acorn, then it sprouts into a seedling, and over years it grows into a tall oak. Finally, the oak drops its own acorns, which connects back to the beginning because a new tree can grow from those acorns and the cycle starts again.

steps: Follow the order words: first, then, finally.
Acorn buried, then sprouts, grows into an oak, then drops acorns.
The dropped acorns can grow into new trees, so the cycle repeats.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Making maple syrup takes patience and care. First, in early spring, farmers drill small holes in maple trees and hang buckets to catch the dripping sap. Next, they collect the watery sap and pour it into a large pan. Then they boil the sap for hours until most of the water disappears. Finally, what is left is thick, sweet maple syrup.

Why must the boiling step come after collecting the sap, and not before?
items.answer: The boiling step must come after collecting because you cannot boil sap you do not have yet. First you gather the watery sap, and only then can you boil it to remove the water and make syrup.

steps: Steps in a procedure depend on the ones before them.
You must first collect the sap from the trees.
Only after you have the sap can you boil it, so boiling must come after collecting.

steps: Follow the chain of causes.

Too many deer ate the young trees, so the riverbanks became bare.
